entities.definition: Fat lobules and uniformly echogenic bands of supporting structures comprise the bulk of breast tissue.
A thick zone of homogeneously echogenic fibroglandular parenchyma is present beneath the isoechoic layer of subcutaneous fat lobules.
The breast echotexture is characterized by multiple small areas of relative increased and decreased echogenicity.
Glandular tissue component <25% of overall fibroglandular tissue.
Glandular tissue component between 25% and 49% of overall fibroglandular tissue.
Glandular tissue component between 50% and 74% of overall fibroglandular tissue.
Glandular tissue component ≥75% of overall fibroglandular tissue.
Elliptical or egg-shaped mass.
Generally oval shape but exhibits one or more indentations resulting in an undulating contour.
Spherical or ball-shaped mass.
Neither oval, lobulated, nor round with acute angle protrusions.
The horizontal dimension of the mass is greater than the anteroposterior dimension in all US orientations.
The anteroposterior dimension of the mass is equal to or greater than the horizontal dimension in any ultrasound orientation.
Well-defined, with a sharp transition between the mass and the surrounding tissue. For a mass to be described as circumscribed at ultrasound, the entire margin must be sharply defined.
Any portion of the margin is non-circumscribed.
All or some portion of the margin is poorly defined or fuzzy with no sharp demarcation from the surrounding tissue.
Some or all of the margin has sharp corners, often forming acute angles.
Characterized by short-cycle 2-3 mm undulations or ripples. Microlobulated describes the margin while lobulated describes the shape of a mass.
Characterized by sharp lines radiating from the mass, often a sign of malignancy.
Without internal echoes.
Having increased echogenicity relative to fat or equal to fibroglandular tissue.
Same echogenicity as subcutaneous fat and may be relatively inconspicuous.
Less echogenic than fat but not anechoic (darker gray than fat but not black).
Displays a mix of echo patterns.
Contains both solid (iso-, hypo-, or hyperechoic) and cystic or fluid (anechoic) components. The important feature is the solid component.
No shadowing or enhancement deep to the mass.
An echogenic column deep to the mass is brighter than that seen in the adjacent tissue at a similar depth.
The area posterior to the mass (shadowing column) is darker than the tissue at the same depth to either side of the mass; edge shadows should be disregarded.
A large geographic area that does not conform to a linear or segmental distribution.
A small, confined area.
A longitudinal area arrayed in a line that may conform to a ductal distribution.
A triangular area with base toward the pectoralis muscle and apex toward the nipple that conforms to a segment of the breast.
Calcifications that are large enough to attenuate the US beam and are typically associated with posterior shadowing.
Tiny echogenic foci on US which are most conspicuous when located within a hypoechoic mass, non-mass lesion or duct.
Calcifications within benign or malignant masses and non-mass lesions depicted on US.
Calcifications situated in fat or fibroglandular tissue which are often less conspicuous than when present within a mass or within a non-mass lesion.
Calcifications within a lactiferous duct.
Thin white line surrounding an otherwise circumscribed margin which must be uniformly thin and, importantly, must be visible around the entire margin of the mass.
A thick echogenic band surrounding all or part of a mass or non-mass lesion which disrupts the texture of the normal tissue surrounding.
Thin lines radiating from a point and/or focal retraction or straightening of the breast parenchyma, representing distortion of tissue planes.

Manifested by cystic dilation of a duct or ducts involving irregularities in caliber and/or arborization, extension of duct(s) to or from a malignant mass, or the presence of an intraductal mass, thrombus, or detritus.
Focal or diffuse skin thickening - more than 2 mm in thickness (up to 4 mm in the periareolar area and inframammary fold).
The skin surface is concave, indented, and appears fixed.
Characterized by interconnected, arborizing hypoechoic or anechoic lines, representing either dilated lymphatics or interstitial fluid.
No vascularity on color or power Doppler.
Blood vessels are present within the finding.
A high number of blood vessels around the margin of a breast abnormality.
The finding stiffness is soft; tend to be benign, though there are exceptions.
Mixed hard and soft stiffness.
Hard stiffness; tend to be malignant, though there are exceptions.
Mass that is circumscribed, round or oval, anechoic, characterized by thin wall and often shows posterior enhancement.
Consists of a cluster of anechoic masses, with thin (<0.5 mm) intervening septations and no discrete solid component within any of the locules.

Characterized by homogeneous low-level internal echoes; may have layered appearance which may shift slowly with changes in the patient's position; may contain echogenic foci that appear to scintillate as they shift.
Clinically apparent masses including sebaceous or epidermal inclusion cysts, keloids, moles, pimples, neurofibromas, and accessory nipples.
May include biopsy marker clips or localization seeds, surgical clips, wires, retained catheter sleeves, cardiac devices, injected or leaked silicone or paraffin, metal or glass related to trauma.
Both silicone and saline within normal implants will appear anechoic with a curvilinear echogenic capsule.

Some changes involve fluid collections (postoperative seromas) that appear entirely cystic or may have septations, internal debris, or contain cystic and solid-appearing components, but should be avascular. Other postsurgical findings, especially scar tissue, may display suspicious findings such as shadowing, hypoechogenicity, irregular shape, spiculated margin, and/or architectural distortion.

Benign inflammatory process from saponification of local fat; on ultrasound has variable appearance depending on phase (acute: increased echogenicity from oedema; subacute: ill-defined complex cystic with low-level echoes; late: calcified walls with posterior shadowing, possible angular/spiculated margins, possible echogenic rim).
Findings consistent with a hematoma in the acute phase that will evolve over time, or fat necrosis which is seen later in the evolution of post-trauma changes.
Typically presents with a palpable breast lump associated with pain, swelling, and erythema.
AVMs (arteriovenous malformations/pseudoaneurysms - usually benign; developmental or acquired) or superficial thrombophlebitis (Mondor's disease - palpable cord with or without pain).

Lymph node within breast tissue. May exist throughout the breast but most commonly in upper outer quadrant (especially axillary tail); may be seen adjacent to blood vessels. Normal size 3-4 mm up to ~1 cm but may be larger. On ultrasound: solid reniform lesion hypoechoic to remainder of breast tissue with well-defined outer margin, hyperechoic central hilar fat, possible hilar blood flow on Doppler. Classified as BI-RADS 2.
Lateral to the lateral margin of the pectoralis minor muscle.
Posterior to the pectoralis minor muscle, or between the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor muscles (also known as interpectoral node or Rotter's node).
Medial to the medial margin of the pectoralis minor muscle.
Lymph node located within internal mammary spaces 1-4, using sternum and ribs as landmarks.
Lymph node in the supraclavicular region. Tumor involvement of ipsilateral supraclavicular node(s) is the highest N stage still confined to regional disease (N3c).
Incomplete assessment: need additional imaging evaluation OR need prior imaging for comparison.
Negative. No finding present in an imaging modality (not even a benign finding), nothing to comment on, normal examination. Essentially 0% likelihood of malignancy.

Benign. Used when the radiologist wants to remark on a benign finding. 100% chance of being benign (essentially 0% likelihood of malignancy). Includes calcified fibroadenomas, secretory calcifications, fat-containing lesions (oil cysts, breast lipomas, galactoceles, mixed-density hamartomas), cutaneous neurofibromas, intramammary lymph nodes, breast sebaceous cysts, simple breast cysts, and breast implants.

Probably benign, with a risk of malignancy of >0% and ≤2%. Reserved for diagnostic setting. Ultrasound findings: complicated cyst with uniform low-level echoes, microlobulated or oval mass composed of clustered microcysts, hypoechoic circumscribed oval parallel mass without posterior features or with minimal posterior enhancement, hyperechoic mass with central hypoechoic-anechoic components and surrounding oedema (consistent with but not diagnostic of fat necrosis), refraction shadowing without associated mass, architectural distortion thought to be due to postsurgical scar.

Suspicious abnormality. May not have characteristic morphology of breast cancer but has definite probability of being malignant. Likelihood of malignancy >2% but <95%. Subclassified into 4A, 4B, and 4C.
Low level of suspicion for malignancy with >2% to ≤10% likelihood of malignancy.
Moderate level of suspicion for malignancy with >10% to ≤50% likelihood of malignancy.
High level of suspicion for malignancy with >50% to <95% likelihood of malignancy.
Highly suggestive of malignancy. Has the characteristic morphology of breast cancer with ≥95% chance of being malignant. If histology is benign, considered discordant with imaging findings.
Known biopsy-proven malignancy. Management is clinical follow-up with surgeon and/or oncologist with definitive local therapy when clinically appropriate.

Common benign breast lesion resulting from excess proliferation of connective tissue, containing both stromal and epithelial cells. On ultrasound: well-circumscribed, round/ovoid/macrolobulated mass with generally uniform hypoechogenicity; intralesional sonographically detectable calcification in ~10%; sometimes thin echogenic pseudocapsule. May mimic phyllodes tumour.

Common benign cause of a breast lump. On ultrasound: oval or round, anechoic, circumscribed margins, posterior acoustic enhancement; may show reverberation artifact, smooth walls, peripheral calcifications. Classified as BI-RADS 2.

Cystic breast lesion showing intracystic debris that may imitate a solid mass. On ultrasound: thin wall with or without posterior acoustic enhancement, homogeneous hypoechoic content, low-level internal echoes that may change shape with patient position, sloping fluid-fluid levels. <2% risk of malignancy; typically classified as BI-RADS 3.

Also known as complex breast cyst. Defined as cyst with thick walls, thick septa, intracystic masses, or other discrete solid components. Classified into four Berg types: type I (thick wall/septa >0.5mm, PPV 7.1%), type II (intracystic with mural lesions, PPV 16.7%), type III (mixed cystic-solid, cystic ≥50%, PPV 61.1%), type IV (predominantly solid ≥50% with cystic foci, PPV 44.8%). 23-31% overall risk of malignancy in some series.

Benign breast lesion where focal fat necrosis becomes walled off by fibrous tissue. On ultrasound: most are hypoechoic with smooth walls, neither posterior acoustic enhancement nor shadowing typically; echogenicity varies; fat-fluid levels possible; rim calcifications can produce posterior shadowing. Complex features include thick walls, mural nodularity, internal echoic bands. Classified as BI-RADS 2.

Benign mesenchymal tumour composed of mature adipose tissue. Predominantly subcutaneous; usually up to 2 cm. On ultrasound: rounded, isoechoic or slightly hyperechoic to surrounding fat, occasionally hypoechoic; thin echogenic septations parallel to skin surface; compressible. Classified as BI-RADS 2.

Retention cyst from lactiferous duct occlusion, most common benign breast lesion in young lactating women. On ultrasound (variable): ~50% cystic/multicystic, ~37% mixed cystic and solid, ~13% solid; lack of blood flow on color Doppler; often subareolar. Classified as BI-RADS 2.
Fat necrosis within days of insult. On ultrasound: increased echogenicity due to oedema of fatty tissue.
Fat necrosis days to months after insult. On ultrasound: ill-defined complex cystic lesion (uni- or multiloculated with low-level echoes) surrounded by oedematous fat.
Fat necrosis 1.5 years or more after insult. On ultrasound: calcified walls with posterior shadowing; if postsurgical, can present as angular margin or spiculated mass with echogenic rim.

Also known as fibroadenolipoma. Benign breast lesion typified by 'breast within a breast' appearance on mammogram. On ultrasound: well-circumscribed solid lesion without intralesional microcalcification; internal echotexture most often mixed hyperechoic and hypoechoic; soft and easy to compress; margins often difficult to delineate because it resembles normal breast tissue. Classified as BI-RADS 2.

Also known as epidermal inclusion cyst or epidermoid cyst. Benign lesion located in skin or subcutaneous tissue with predilection for inframammary fold. On ultrasound: small, hypoechoic, located close to skin surface with through transmission, no detectable vascular flow; alternating hypo- and hyperechoic rings; may show track extending to skin surface; Doppler may show remarkable flow if low-grade infection. Classified as BI-RADS 2.

Part of the spectrum of cystic change in the breast on ultrasound. On ultrasound: cluster of anechoic foci, each less than 2-3 mm in diameter, with thin (<0.5 mm) intervening septations and no discrete solid components. No malignant potential.

Devices placed in the breast for augmentation or reconstruction. On ultrasound: both silicone and saline within normal implants appear anechoic with a curvilinear echogenic capsule. Classified as BI-RADS 2.
Berg complex cyst type I: masses with a thick wall (>0.5 mm) or thick septa (>0.5 mm). PPV for malignancy 7.1%.
Berg complex cyst type II: masses of an intracystic type with one or more discrete solid mural lesions within a cyst. PPV for malignancy 16.7%.
Berg complex cyst type III: masses containing mixed cystic and solid components with the cystic portion occupying at least 50% of the mass. PPV for malignancy 61.1%.
Berg complex cyst type IV: masses that are predominantly (at least 50%) solid with eccentric or central cystic foci. PPV for malignancy 44.8%.
Rare benign fat-containing breast lesion that appears hyperechoic on ultrasound.
Benign collection from acute haemorrhage in the breast; appears hyperechoic on ultrasound in acute phase.
Benign vascular lesion of the breast that can contain hyperechoic components on ultrasound.
Benign fibrous lesion of the breast that can appear hyperechoic on ultrasound.
Synonym for breast hamartoma. Benign fat-containing breast lesion that can appear hyperechoic on ultrasound.

relations.definition: Asserts a taxonomic relationship: the subject is a kind of the object.
Asserts that the subject is a more specific category falling under the object.
Asserts that the subject is a component or part of the object.
Indicates that the subject feature, when present, is associated with malignant lesions in breast ultrasound interpretation.
relations.notes: Use 'specificity' field (high/medium/low) to indicate strength of association.

relations.definition: Indicates that the subject feature, when present, is associated with benign lesions in breast ultrasound interpretation.
relations.notes: Use 'specificity' field (high/medium/low) to indicate strength of association.

relations.definition: Indicates the feature is observed in malignant lesions.
Indicates the feature is observed in benign lesions.
Qualifies how strongly a feature predicts malignancy. Values: high, medium, low.
Indicates the BI-RADS category that the subject lesion is typically assigned.
Asserts a BI-RADS category assignment.
Indicates that the subject BI-RADS subcategory is a refinement of the object BI-RADS category.
A specific percentage or qualitative value of the probability of malignancy associated with the subject.
A range of percentage values for the probability of malignancy associated with the subject.
A minimum percentage threshold of malignancy probability for the subject.
Indicates that the object is one of the recognized descriptors under the subject feature category.
Indicates that the subject is a descriptor falling under the object category in the BI-RADS lexicon hierarchy.
Asserts that a combination of features (named in the subject as a compound feature string) indicates the object diagnosis or category.
Asserts that the object descriptor is part of the typical ultrasound appearance of the subject lesion.
Indicates that the subject lesion can appear similar to the object on ultrasound, posing diagnostic confusion.
Indicates that the object lesion is in the differential diagnosis when the subject lesion is considered.
Asserts that the subject is visible on the object imaging modality.
Asserts that the subject is an imaging artifact produced by the object.
Asserts a typical anatomic location for the subject.
Asserts a frequent but non-exclusive location for the subject.
Indicates a non-causal association between the subject feature and the object.
Maps a category to its canonical short name or descriptor (e.g., birads_1 → negative).
Maps a BI-RADS category to its recommended management action.
relations.notes: Used only for the BI-RADS 0 row; otherwise management content was skipped per scope.

relations.definition: Asserts that the subject finding indicates the object condition or diagnosis.
Asserts that the subject finding can be produced by the object underlying entity.
Asserts a synonym relationship between two terms.
Asserts that the subject and object are distinct entities in differential diagnosis on ultrasound.
relations.notes: Weaker than 'mimics' which implies confusion; 'differs_from' explicitly contrasts.

relations.definition: Maps a lesion to its typical size range on ultrasound.
Asserts that the subject lesion has no malignant potential.
Indicates that the subject finding category has an associated feature (object) that increases predicted malignancy risk.
Indicates that the subject finding, when present alongside a suspicious mass, supports the diagnosis of malignancy.
Indicates that the subject finding suggests a BI-RADS 5 classification (≥95% likelihood of malignancy).
Indicates that the subject ultrasound finding suggests the lesion is solid rather than cystic.
Indicates that the subject finding specifically suggests a simple cyst diagnosis (benign).
